name: Elliptical
pattern: Standing gait on two pedals that trace an oval: feet never leave the pedals, arms push and pull the handles opposite the legs.
setup: Step on with the pedals still, holding the fixed bars.
Whole foot on the pedal, toes forward, feet hip width.
Then move your hands to the moving handles at chest height.

steps.text: Right pedal forward and up, left pedal back; left hand pulls, right hand pushes.
Press the right pedal down and back through the whole foot.
Switch: left pedal forward, right pedal back.
Press the left pedal down and back. Keep a smooth, even rhythm.

cues.cue: Stand tall over the pedals, shoulders over hips.
cues.why: Leaning on the rails takes body weight off the legs and lowers the work done.

cues.cue: Keep the whole foot down; let the heel lift only a little at the back.
cues.why: Up on the toes loads the calves and can numb the feet.

cues.cue: Knees track over the toes, soft, never locked.
cues.why: Elliptical knee motion stays more bent than in walking; locking loses that.

cues.cue: Push and pull the handles; do not just rest on them.
cues.why: Active arms add upper-body work and raise the energy cost.

breathing: Breathe steadily through the nose and mouth in time with your stride.

tempo.note: About 50-70 revolutions a minute; harder by resistance or incline, not just speed.

mistakes.name: Leaning on the rails
mistakes.looks: Elbows locked on the bars, body bent forward, weight in the hands.
mistakes.fix: Hands light on the moving handles, chest up.
mistakes.why: Supporting body weight through the arms cuts the leg work and calories, and rounds the back.

mistakes.name: Up on the toes
mistakes.looks: Heels lift high off the pedals the whole time.
mistakes.fix: Drive through the heel and midfoot.
mistakes.why: Calves tire early and feet go numb.

mistakes.name: Too fast, no resistance
mistakes.looks: Legs spin with no load and the body bobs.
mistakes.fix: Add resistance until each push feels firm.
mistakes.why: Momentum does the work and the effort drops.

safety: Step on and off only when the pedals are still.
Knee pain: lower the incline and keep the knees soft.

variants.change: Hands off: arms swing as in walking, more balance work.

motion.basis: Direction of differences from walking (more hip and pelvic motion, knee curve shifted to more flexion) from damiano2011 and lu2007 (cadence about 52 rpm in that study); the degree values are estimates.

sources.cite: American College of Sports Medicine. ACSM's Guidelines for Exercise Testing and Prescription, 11th ed. Wolters Kluwer, 2021.
